mechanism_narrative: A low level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as lower discount rates increase the present value of future equity cash flows, and this relationship holds across all monetary regimes.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (as measured by the 20-day return sign), or the Rank IC over a 5-year rolling window falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5% in a 3-month window, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 45% of triggered periods (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS not rising) signals an accommodative stance that fails to curb inflation, leading to negative equity returns as the market anticipates future rate hikes.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (CPIAUCSL rising and FEDFUNDS stable) does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a non-significant coefficient (p>0.05) over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) exceeds 6.0%, it indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns during the high-unemployment regime.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 6.0%, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 45% of cases, or the average return in high-unemployment periods is not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong housing market (HOUST) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as rising home construction signals robust consumer spending and economic growth, which supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is above its 10-year moving average, or the Rank IC over a 5-year window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95.0% of its 12-month peak, it signals a manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 45% of triggered periods (INDPRO < 95.0% of 12-month peak), or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong consumer spending (RSAFS) and weak industrial output (INDPRO) signals a demand-led slowdown where consumption is not supported by production capacity, leading to negative equity returns as the market anticipates reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: The interaction (RSAFS rising and INDPRO falling) does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a non-significant coefficient (p>0.05) over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high consumer spending regime (RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive as robust retail activity supports corporate earnings growth, but this effect is only significant during economic expansions.
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS > 500000, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 45% of cases, or the average return in high-spending periods is not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).
